findings: Per-unit floor: 0.46 mean blind accuracy across the unit's five questions (0.55, 0.50, 0.36, 0.52, 0.38), 1.85x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option sets visible, all five questions of the unit visible together. This is a no-passage-with-options figure; nothing in this pipeline measures a prompts-alone quantity and I did not estimate one.

Form profile: word counts 16/14/16/15, all active, no negation, no hedges anywhere. Convergent isolate on A: it is the only option with three clauses, the only one carrying an evaluative judgement ("so eleven is a good figure"), and the only one containing a bare numeral. Repair: drop the evaluative tail and the numeral from A, or give the other three comparable specificity.

Reversal pair: A is the direction-reversed twin of C on one variable, whether the recorded number rises or falls as the odorant weakens. A student who spots the reversal narrows to A and C. Repair: build the nearest neighbour of the key out of a different variable.

Responsiveness split: A and C open "They" and describe the numbers, which is what the prompt asks about; B and D open "He" and describe the man. Repair: make all four describe the numbers, or all four describe the procedure.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE route, expert-only: C restates the standard odorant sniff-test measurement, the share of gas in air at first detection, so a reader with gas-industry knowledge selects it cold. Repair: key the question to a passage-specific value or condition rather than the generic definition.

CROSS_QUESTION support: Q3's options discuss readings and smell that "goes missing on the way", corroborating the detection-threshold reading of Q1. Repair: keep the nature of the measurement out of sibling questions' options.
Student-available portion reaches only about 0.40 (form isolate on A plus prompt responsiveness); the remainder is expert. Verdict is flag, but it sits near the line and should be read as near-kill.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.55. Channels: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only), CROSS_QUESTION, PAIR_STRUCTURE via the A/C reversal. Below the 0.60 kill line because the part of the route that would carry a student, rather than a gas engineer, tops out near 0.40.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION removal, student-available: D says the odorant "reaches the house more or less intact and is lost at the cooker instead", but Q5's prompt establishes that the date for lighting the houses is still only set, so no cooker is in use. Repair: drop the cooker or attribute the claim to an estate already in service.
Same leak, weaker, on C: "once the steel has begun to corrode in service" is off-frame for a run not yet in service. Repair: reword C so it concerns new pipe.
Prompt fit: the prompt asks what happens to the compound; B answers where the compound is added, which is not a fate. Repair: make B a competing fate, for example that it is stripped at a filter.

Form profile: NO convergent isolate. Counts 14/16/14/15, every option opens "It", no negation, no absolutizers; two hedged (A "partly" and "hardly", D "more or less") against two flat, which is the prescribed balance and does not score. Voice splits 2+2. Nothing to repair on form.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE route, expert-only: A is the textbook account of odorant fade, the carrier partly oxidised to a far weaker-smelling compound. Repair: give C, the adsorption account, equally textbook shape so domain knowledge cannot separate the two.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.50. Channels: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only), CROSS_QUESTION (student-available, removes D and weakly C). C survives as a live rival because adsorption is as real a mechanism as oxidation, which is what holds this below a kill.

findings: Form profile: counts 14/15/17/16, all open "It", no negation, no absolutizers. Convergent isolate on B: the only epistemic hedge ("probably"), the only passive main verb ("was probably laid"), and the only cleft ("which is what keeps its readings down"). Repair: de-hedge B or hedge a second option, and match B's main-clause voice to the set.

Content removal of the same option: a narrower bore raises the surface-to-volume ratio and would cost more odorant per unit length, not less, so B is backwards. Two independent removals of one option lift a student from 0.25 to 0.33 before any reading. Repair: make B's physics defensible.
No selection route beyond that removal: A (short line, little loss) and D (old line, long since conditioned) are both live and I cannot separate them cold. The item's residual difficulty is real.
Repair priority: fix B only. A, C and D are well matched in length, opening and register.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.36 on the reading that an old conditioned line is the contrast a pickling text needs; the tilt over A is thin. Channel: form-profile isolate on B (student-available) plus expert-only physics confirming the same removal. Flag rather than pass because the removal route is real and doubly confirmed; flag rather than kill because nothing selects among the remaining three.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION removal of two of four options, fully student-available and the most repairable defect in the unit. First: Q5's prompt speaks of "the date set for lighting the houses", so the houses are not yet in use and D ("carried out once the houses on the run are in use") is out. Second: Q5's options A and D both presuppose "the heavy dose", so A ("at the ordinary dose") is out. Repair: change D's condition and A's dose so neither contradicts the unit's own established timeline.
Intra-question reinforcement of the same removal: C presupposes "the fortnight of extra smell", which contradicts A's ordinary dose inside a single option set. Repair: remove one of the two.

Form profile: counts 16/16/18/18, no negation, no hedges. Convergent isolate on C: the only option not opening with the pronoun "It" (it opens "Its main cost") and the only absolutizer ("as short as possible"). Repair: rewrite C to the set's shape.

Net effect: a test-wise student who reads Q5 before answering Q4 sits at 0.50 between B and C with no passage, and near 0.55-0.60 if the form isolate on C is also used. This item should be rebuilt before the unit ships.
justification: Blind pick B at 0.52. Channels: CROSS_QUESTION (student-available, two removals), form-profile isolate on C. The B-over-C tie-break needs the expert judgement that odorant cost is not what limits a pickle, so the student-available floor is about 0.50 and the verdict is flag, at the top of the flag band.

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN / PAIR_STRUCTURE, student-available: A and D are the only options that reuse the text's phrase "the heavy dose" and the only pair opposed on one variable, whether the date stands or has slipped; B and C sit off that axis. A student who narrows on the shared phrase is at 0.50 with no passage. Repair: put the shared phrase in all four options or in none.

Off-axis options are weak on their own terms: B introduces "the council", an entity absent from the other three, and is the only future-tense option; C splits the date across houses, which no other option contemplates. Repair: make all four positions on one schedule variable.
The four options otherwise form a graded exclusivity cluster on a single continuum (stands, mostly stands, slipped a week, abandoned). Per calibration that cluster is inert and I did not score it.
Form profile: NO convergent isolate. Counts 16/16/15/15, all open "It", no negation, no absolutizers, no epistemic hedges. The leak here is lexical repetition, not form.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.38, and the tilt over A comes only from narrative shape, which is not a route a student can execute. The student-available route is the A/D narrowing at 0.50, which is what earns the flag.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.25 mean blind accuracy across all five gaps, 1.00x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option sets visible, all five questions visible together. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.
This unit is the batch's clean control. The prompt "Gap (1)" carries no information at all, so the only possible channel is the option set itself, and the option sets are bare single words.

"Nowadays" is the only temporal adverb and "Worse" the only comparative: two single-variable isolates pointing at different options, which cancel per calibration. Three stance markers against one temporal adverb is a 3+1 cluster and is inert.
No repair required.
justification: Blind pick A is an unguided guess; confidence is base. No WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, ENTAILMENT, PAIR_STRUCTURE or CROSS_QUESTION route exists without the passage.

findings: Form profile collapses: four bare person-nouns, one word each, no isolate on any prescribed variable.
"caretaker" and "lodger" share a housing field against "witness" and "recruit". That is a 2+2 field split, not a contradiction on one variable, and it narrows nothing without the sentence.

justification: Blind pick D is an unguided guess; confidence is base.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.55 for this single-question unit, 2.20x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option set visible. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.

Form profile: counts 19/16/18/17, all flat except C's "will" and D's "have to", no negation, no absolutizers. Convergent isolate on B: the only option without a coordinated second clause, the only one with an indefinite generic subject ("A small instrument") against "Her meter", "The cold hall" and "The last notes", and the shortest at 16. Repair: give B a scene-anchored two-clause shape like the others.

Worst case: the form isolate and the content-favoured option are the same option. B is also what WORLD_KNOWLEDGE selects, since a small piano's inharmonicity exceeds a generic stretch curve, which is the textbook reason for stretching past a meter's figure. A form reader and a physics reader converge. Repair: make one distractor equally generic and equally physically plausible.

Prompt fit, partly student-available: the prompt names the meter's curve, and only A and B mention the meter or "the figure"; C and D give meter-independent reasons. Narrowing on prompt fit puts a student near 0.40 on B. Repair: have every option engage the meter, or none.
Single question, so no pair structure and no cross-question channel is available here.
justification: Blind pick B at 0.55. Channels: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only at full strength), ENTAILMENT via prompt fit (student-available, about 0.40), form-profile isolate on B. Flag not kill because the student-available portion does not reach 0.60 on its own.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.38 for this single-question unit, 1.52x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option set visible. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.

Form profile: counts 15/16/16/14, all open with a determiner, no hedges, no negation. Convergent isolate on D: the only single-clause option, the only absolutizer ("the biggest crowd of any on the card"), and the shortest. It is also an unsupportable claim type, since a card of days cannot imply crowd size. Two independent removals put a student at 0.33 before reading. Repair: drop the superlative and match D's clause structure to the set.
Single-variable isolate on C (the only passive, "is shared") points at a different option than D's isolate and therefore cancels; I did not score it.

Weak PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and B are opposed on one variable, whether market days or the coach road governed the card, with C and D off that axis. This is 1+1, not a 2+2 contradiction, so it scores only as a mild narrowing.

Common-sense route, partly student-available: that an itinerant weekly round follows the towns' market days is inferable without the essay. Repair: make the key turn on something only the essay supplies, such as a named exception to the market-day order.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.38. A and B are close enough that I cannot call the unit; the defensible finding is the removal of D and the mild A/B narrowing. Flag.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.52 mean blind accuracy across the unit's four questions (0.62, 0.50, 0.45, 0.50), 2.07x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option sets visible, all four questions of the unit visible together. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.

KILL route, student-available: an eye chart's rows shrink by a constant proportion, so the largest absolute drop falls between the two top rows and the bottom rows are nearly equal. ”Höjden minskar mest mellan de två översta raderna.” follows from the everyday picture of a syntavla alone, with no passage and no expertise. Repair: key the question to a numeric schedule the text must supply, or ask about a row pair the picture cannot settle.

CROSS_QUESTION reinforcement: Q2's options establish that the sheet is proportionally spaced (C: ”Störningen växer när mellanrummet är litet i förhållande till bokstaven.”; D: ”Trängseln avtar nedåt på arket i takt med att bokstäverna krymper.”), which settles this question's geometry from a sibling option set. Repair: keep the sheet's scaling out of Q2's options.

A is the linear-decrement trap; B, C and D are a three-way exclusivity cluster on which row pair drops most. That 3+1 cluster is inert per calibration and I did not score it. The kill comes entirely from world knowledge, not from structure.

Form profile: NO isolate, and the set is exemplary. All four options are 8 words, all open ”Höjden”, all active, no negation, no hedges, no absolutizers, and B, C and D are identical through the run ”Höjden minskar mest mellan de två”, differing only in the final positional phrase. The repair must be to content; there is nothing to fix in the shape.
justification: Blind pick B at 0.62. Kill, and the only kill in the batch. The route is WORLD_KNOWLEDGE of a kind every Swedish student has in the form of a remembered image, reinforced by CROSS_QUESTION leakage from Q2, so it is student-available rather than expert-only. It sits just over the 0.60 line and the coordinator should treat that boundary as soft, but the option set cannot be rescued by rewriting shape.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE route, partly student-available: C states the crowding rule in its standard form, that interference grows as the gap shrinks relative to the letter, and reads as self-evident even to a reader who has never met the rule. Repair: make the key require a passage-specific figure.
B is removable cold: spaces do not impair the eye's resolution of a character, so the option is internally confused. Repair: make B a coherent competitor.

D is removable by CROSS_QUESTION against Q1's proportional geometry: if the sheet scales, crowding does not fall down the sheet. Repair: as for Q1, do not let the sheet's scaling be recoverable from sibling option sets.
A is a live rival and is also true of real charts, since proportional inter-letter spacing does take crowding into account. Keeping A is what holds this question below a kill; do not weaken it.

Form profile: NO convergent isolate. Counts 9/10/10/11, all active, all flat, no negation or absolutizers. A is isolated only on its genitive opening (”Tavlans typografi”), a single variable with nothing converging on it.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.50. Channels: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, CROSS_QUESTION. Student-available floor about 0.40 after removing B and D; flag.

findings: Form profile: counts 13/10/10/10, no negation, no absolutizers. Convergent isolate on A: longest by three words, the only human subject (”Barnet”), and the only option with the modal ”får”. Repair: match A's length and subject to the set.
MIRRORED_TWIN: C and D both open ”Bokstäverna”, which brackets the pair a narrowing student will keep. Repair: vary the openings or give all four the same one.

ENTAILMENT route, student-available: the prompt is a cleft asking what takes time, and D (”en bokstav i taget”) is the only option naming a per-unit procedure, which is the generic answer to that question shape. Repair: give B the same per-unit shape, or drop the cleft from the prompt.
C's ”än förut” imports Q4's chart-change frame into this question and tells a student the unit turns on a change of sheet. Repair: remove the comparative.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.45. Channels: ENTAILMENT via question shape (student-available), form-profile isolate removing A, plus expert knowledge that per-letter scoring is the known time cost of this chart type. Flag.

findings: ENTAILMENT / prompt-fit narrowing, student-available: the prompt asks how the text describes the change, and A and D are descriptive while B (”visar att”) and C (”beror på”) are explanatory. Matching the prompt's verb to the option's verb narrows to two. Repair: make all four descriptive or all four explanatory.

B is removable on instinct: an essay built around a change of sheet does not conclude that children's eyesight simply improved. Repair: make B compatible with the artifact reading so it is not self-defeating.

Shared presupposition across option sets: A's ”bytesåret” and C's ”det nya arket”, together with Q3's ”än förut”, let a student recover the fact of the chart change without the passage, which is the premise the whole unit turns on. Repair: presuppose the change in one option only.
Form profile: NO convergent isolate. All four open ”Den”; counts 13/10/12/14; D carries the only explicit negation (”och inte i de andra”), a single-variable isolate with nothing converging on it.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.50. Channels: ENTAILMENT via prompt fit, CROSS_QUESTION via the shared presupposition. Student-available floor about 0.40-0.45; flag.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.29 mean blind accuracy across the unit's two questions (0.30, 0.28), 1.16x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option sets visible, both questions of the unit visible together. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.

Near base, and close to clean. A, C and D are three positions on one variable, how the order between cars is settled, with B outside it. That 3+1 exclusivity cluster is inert per calibration and I did not score it.

Two cross-cutting oppositions cancel: A against B on capacity (share the current that exists versus raise the main fuse) and C against D on process (defer the ordering versus settle it at the meeting). They point at different options and hand a student nothing.

Mild form asymmetry: A is the longest at 16 words against 12/14/14 and the most embedded, carrying both a purpose clause and a relative clause, while all four share the modal bör and a definite-noun opening. Repair: trim A. This is a shape defect, not an answerability leak.

A domain prior exists but does not select: load balancing is the standard Swedish recommendation precisely to avoid raising the main fuse, which tilts against B as the writer's stance while saying nothing about which of A, C and D the writer holds.
justification: Blind pick C at 0.30, essentially base. No channel carried me; the pick rests on the weak template expectation that a stance question is keyed to the qualified position. Pass.

findings: The four options are not mutually exclusive: a notice can sit behind glass and give the proposal half a page and place it seventh. There is no cluster logic and no contradiction to exploit. This is good design and should be preserved.

Form profile: counts 6/6/6/7, all open ”Den”, all active, no negation, no absolutizers. Convergent isolate on D: the only option with a subordinate clause, the only one with a modal (”ska”), and the longest. Repair: flatten D to the set's shape.
Minor and cancelling: A is the only option that does not name the proposal, a single-variable isolate pointing at a different option than D's, so the two cancel and I scored neither as selective.
No WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, ENTAILMENT or CROSS_QUESTION route. Nothing in Q1 discloses anything about the notice.
justification: Blind pick B at 0.28, essentially base. The only finding is the shape of D. Pass.

findings: Per-unit floor: 0.37 mean blind accuracy across the unit's two questions (0.32, 0.42), 1.48x the 0.25 base. Condition: no passage, full option sets visible, both questions of the unit visible together. No-passage-with-options figure; no prompts-alone quantity is measured or estimated.

Strongest form isolate in the batch: C is isolated on four prescribed variables at once. It is the shortest at 6 words against 7/8/8, the only option with no subordinate clause, the only explicit negation, carried morphologically in ”omålat”, and the only absolutizer (”båda sidor”). Repair: give C a subordinate clause, drop ”båda”, and match its length to the set.

The isolate's direction is ambiguous and that is itself the problem. Most test-wise readers will discount C as the too-short, too-absolute option, but a plainly stated fact also produces a short option, so C may be the key. The shape biases the set whichever way it is keyed, so it needs repair even though I did not convert it into a lift for my own pick.
MIRRORED_TWIN: B (”så utsatt att”) and D (”så lågt att”) share one frame while A and C do not. Repair: use the frame in all four options or in none.
No content route: A, B and D are all live descriptions of an old open-air dance floor's railing and I cannot separate them cold.
justification: Blind pick D at 0.32, barely above base. Channel: form-profile isolate on C, which removes at most one option and does so in an ambiguous direction. Flag on the strength of the four-variable convergence, not on any lift toward my pick.

findings: Student-available removal: B explains the floor's shape by a roof post in the middle of the dance floor (”en stolpe mitt på golvet”), which any reader rejects as an obstruction to dancing. Repair: move the post to a perimeter ring so the option is not self-defeating.

Cultural route, partly student-available: that couples circulate one way around a floor, which suits a round bana, is common knowledge in Sweden, so A is reachable without the passage. Repair: make the key turn on a detail only the text supplies.
A, B and C all explain a round plan while D explains a cambered section. That 3+1 exclusivity cluster is inert per calibration and I did not score it.

Form profile: NO convergent isolate. All four open ”Den”, all past tense, all active, no hedges or modals. A is isolated only on clause structure, as the only option with a second independent clause, and D only on length at 14 words against 11/12/10; these point at different options and cancel.

A's second clause adds a separate evaluative claim about cost that the key would also have to carry. Repair: split that claim off, since a two-part option is either doubly supported or doubly refutable.
justification: Blind pick A at 0.42. Channels: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE of a common-cultural rather than expert kind, plus the student-available removal of B. Flag.

findings: RULE 15 pair analysis, both legs. Leg one (Q1, the writer's stance): floor 0.30. Leg two (Q2, the notice): floor 0.28. Both legs carry form-only findings; neither has a content route.
Independent product: 0.30 x 0.28 = 0.084, which is 1.34x the 6.25% pair base.

Correlation-adjusted: no channel spans the legs. There is no fact whose recovery answers both, no shared presupposition that transfers, and the option sets share only topic nouns. Taking rho at about 0.05 for a faint topic halo, 0.084 + 0.05 x sqrt(0.30 x 0.70 x 0.28 x 0.72) = 0.094, which is 1.51x base.

Which is honest: for this unit the independent product is the honest figure, because the legs genuinely are independent. The adjustment moves it by one point and I report 0.094 only to show the adjustment was performed, not because a shared channel exists. In general the correlation-adjusted figure is the honest one, since blind pair success is usually driven by a single reconstruction paying off twice; this unit is the exception that shows the adjustment is being computed rather than assumed.
Condition on both figures: no passage, full option sets visible, both questions of the unit visible together. No-passage-with-options figures; no prompts-alone pair quantity is measured or estimated.
No pair-level repair required. The per-question repairs, principally the shape of Q2's option D, stand on their own.
justification: Joint blind floor 0.094 against a 6.25% base, 1.51x. Pass at the pair level.

findings: RULE 15 pair analysis, both legs. Leg one (Q1, the railing): floor 0.32, set by the four-variable form isolate on C, which removes at most one option in an ambiguous direction. Leg two (Q2, the floor's shape): floor 0.42, set by the student-available removal of B plus a common-cultural tilt to A.
Independent product: 0.32 x 0.42 = 0.134, which is 2.15x the 6.25% pair base.

Correlation-adjusted: one channel spans both legs. Both questions are answered from a single reconstructed picture, an old open-air dance floor with a roof on perimeter supports, a low perimeter rail and a floor that sheds rain, and the same picture that rejects a post in the middle of the floor for Q2 suggests a low perimeter rail for Q1. Taking rho at about 0.30, 0.134 + 0.30 x sqrt(0.32 x 0.68 x 0.42 x 0.58) = 0.203, which is 3.25x base.

Which is honest: the correlation-adjusted figure. The independent product understates the joint by roughly a third whenever one mental model pays off on both legs, and this unit is exactly that case; treating the legs as independent here would report 2.15x for a unit that actually sits at 3.25x.
Condition on both figures: no passage, full option sets visible, both questions of the unit visible together. No-passage-with-options figures; no prompts-alone pair quantity is measured or estimated.

Pair-level repair: make the two legs draw on different facets of the text. Keep one question on the physical object and move the other onto something the reconstructed picture cannot supply, such as who built or paid for the bana, or when it stopped being used.
justification: Joint blind floor 0.203 against a 6.25% base, 3.25x, on the correlation-adjusted figure that I judge honest. Flag at the pair level, driven by a shared reconstruction rather than by either leg alone.
